4:09 - This panning to the side along with how coherent it stays despite how much the camera is turning and rotating to the side is making me think that they have a teqhnique of having a mix of low poly generated 3D models and coherent AI generation of image onto it, that explains how they are able to capture different angles from the same scene + being able to have such consistant and convincing 3D correct angles for objects in space (maybe it even explains how it is able to simulate - litterally simulate physics, maybe through the same invisible 3D scene it constructed the generation of video upon) -
--------------------------------
 Edit : also, note how the camera can move perfectly smooth on its own yet the content itself that is viewed is sometimes kind of low frame rate, that's also making sense for it to be based on 3D because it means that the camera view angle is separate from the content of generation (else the same framerate would have been applied to both the camera motion and the object that is moving in it for example and this is not the case here)
--------------------------------
Another thing is that maybe bcs it's based on 3D scene then it's making it easier for the AI model to understand where to put lighting and reflections in a coherent way since it already exist's as 3D surfaces in different angle's ETC so then that's also why it can make it look so coherent with it's lighting and reflections as well, maybe their model is trained to know how to allucinate images coherently in relation to 3d space it has to work with in a 3d scene

📝 Summary of Key Points:

📌 The video introduces Sora, an AI model developed by OpenAI that can create realistic and imaginative scenes from simple text instructions, generating videos based on prompts like describing humans, cities, animals, landscapes, and more.

🧐 Sora is capable of creating videos up to a minute long, maintaining visual quality and adhering to user prompts accurately. It can understand and simulate complex scenes with multiple characters, specific motions, and accurate details of subjects and backgrounds.

🚀 Sora uses a diffusion model to generate videos, gradually transforming noise into coherent visuals. It builds on past research in AI models like GPT to understand and interpret text instructions effectively, enabling it to create compelling characters and scenes.

💡 Additional Insights and Observations:

💬 The video showcases how Sora can bring text prompts to life with stunning visuals, demonstrating its ability to create diverse and imaginative scenarios as requested by users.
📊 Sora's weaknesses include challenges in accurately simulating complex physics scenes and understanding specific cause-and-effect instances, indicating areas for further improvement in AI video generation.

📣 Concluding Remarks:

The advancement of AI models like Sora by OpenAI represents a significant leap in text-to-video capabilities, offering a glimpse into the future of creative content generation. With the potential to revolutionize storytelling, filmmaking, and animation, Sora's ability to understand and simulate the physical world through text prompts opens up new possibilities for artists and creators. Sora embodies the fusion of creativity and technology, democratizing video creation and challenging us to envision a future where imagination knows no bounds.

However, Sora also brings to the forefront the need for ethical contemplation in AI's evolution. OpenAI's engagement with a broad community underscores its commitment to responsible innovation. As Sora paves the way for a new realm of creative expression, it compels us to reflect on the broader implications of our creations, promoting a future where technology enhances creativity responsibly and inclusively.

comments.author: @marcuscarana9240
comments.text:
This is a long read so feel free to skip and enjoy your day.

But here are my takes on the subject.

As crisp and hyperrealistic these A.I. generated videos are. They all still look very generic. They look like stock images and stock photos and I've seen this problem with A.I. generated images where the most realistic looking results looks very similar to each other. For scenes like this 2:26 and this 12:25 which look way more unique and interesting, it does look very amateurish. And then when we go to even more bizarre uncharted land like in this image 3:39, it becomes even more clunky and fake looking. So if the goal is generating a crisp and hyperrealistic but very generic image or video, then yes the A.I. is very good at that. But if you're looking to generate something more unique, more out of this world, the results gets to be less impressive, almost amateurish looking. 

Another problem I have with this is that these aren't A.I. "art", they aren't A.I."animations". Calling yourself an artist or an animator, when you are essentially just a prompt button pusher asking a robot to do something for you because you can't do it yourself is just not a good approach at being creative, original or trying to be something new. So no, I heavily disagree that this will allow people to be able to make more original creations than what Hollywood is already pumping out these days. A lot of A.I. generated comics and webtoons rarely have a positive rating, with most of them having very negative reviews, mainly because of how the character design keeps changing in each panel, terrain and perspective isn't consistent and that's because it really boils down to relying on a software that is just basically guessing what the prompt wants to have.

comments.text:
This is impressive, but the current AIs are still a long way from having agency and self awareness.  They don't know what people are, they don't know what videos are, they don't know the difference between "true" and "false" - they don't have any sensory inputs of their own and don't have a brain equivalent.  So yes, they're getting better at pattern recognition and manipulation - but they don't have anywhere near the computational capacity of a human brain, and lack the equivalents of the specialized hard wired processing for making sense out of their surroundings that human brains have. They can mimic people, but there is no person there.  Roth says they "understand" things, and "think about"things - that's not what's going on here. 

As this video narration shows, people are treating AIs more and more as if they are thinking in a general intelligence way - but they're not, they're a completely different thing.  There's no person there.
